projects.name: ChemInventory
projects.summary: Chemical inventory that fits how each lab works. One record of what a lab holds, where it is and who changed it.
points: Tracks chemicals, locations, orders and batch documents.
Keeps a change history with the user and the time.
Gives each person a role: admin, manager or chemist.
projects.note: The demo uses sample data. Changes reset on refresh.

preview.alt: The ChemInventory demo: a table of chemicals with product number, batch, name, CAS number and actions.

backlink.placement: Footer of cheminventory.co, below the copyright line.

projects.name: Bench Bridge
projects.summary: A demo of how older lab instruments can feed a laboratory information management system (LIMS) and a controlled-substance ledger.
points: Concept drawings show the tap hardware for each instrument.
projects.note: Runs in your browser with sample data and a mock LIMS. No real instrument is connected.

preview.alt: Bench Bridge: a drawing of an analytical balance with a tap, the instrument list, and the five pipeline steps.

backlink.placement: Top bar, left of the fleet card. It shows an arrow and the words. On a narrow window it shows the arrow only.

projects.name: dcurves
projects.summary: A Python package for decision curve analysis. The method evaluates and compares prediction models and diagnostic tests by their clinical consequences.
points: Evaluates models for binary and survival outcomes.
Calculates net benefit and interventions avoided.
projects.note: Shaun created dcurves. The repository belongs to the MSKCC-Epi-Bio organization on GitHub.

projects.name: bioeq
projects.summary: A Python package for bioequivalence analysis. It handles 2x2 crossover, parallel and replicate designs.

projects.name: hct-equity
projects.summary: Models that compare survival predictions across race groups, with calibration and decision curve analysis. It uses synthetic data from a Kaggle competition. It is not peer reviewed.
